title: Signing-ceremony anomaly layer (#600) made concrete: S-SRAM intent fingerprint, 'CHANGED SINCE LAST ATTEMPT' diff page, per-session repeat cap
threat: Error-mimicry: the companion reports 'failed, sign again' and re-submits a mutated payload (recipient, amount, slot, chain) until the user stops reading; the trusted display defeats substitution but not attention exhaustion. threat-model.md:282 records 'NONE TODAY'.
proposal: Keep in S-SRAM (reset on lock) the last K=4 rendered-intent fingerprints: `sha256(dialog kind || every rendered page's bytes)` plus the decoded salient fields (to, value/amount, token, chain_id, slot) and a timestamp. On the next sign request: if a fingerprint matches within 10 min, show a 'REPEAT #n of same request' banner and after n ≥ 3 require scroll-to-end plus a 2-s hold; if the salient fields differ from the most recent attempt within the window, prepend a mandatory 'CHANGED SINCE LAST ATTEMPT: <field old -> new>' page before the normal pages. Cap identical-intent re-prompts per unlock session (e.g. 5) with a refusal that names the reason; since F-17 already limits 250 signs/session, reuse its counters. Add a QEMU e2e that mutates the recipient between two signs and asserts the diff page is rendered.
rationale: This is the one companion-substitution attack the trusted display does not address, and pq1 already has everything needed (page builders produce byte-exact pages; `ui-capture` hashes frames). Trezor's `ContinueOnErrors` stops honouring host cancellation after an error; none of the vendors render a diff — a cheap, visible 'beyond' feature.

risks: False positives on legitimate retries (gas bump re-submits differ only in fee fields — exclude fee fields from the diff or label them); S-SRAM footprint (~K x 200 B); page-budget interaction with `MAX_PAGES` and the ui-px scroll-to-end gate; must not persist anything to flash (invariant: no new per-signature flash state).
